audit.page: Scoped re-audit: ownership note on fleet, thread and signin
audit.method: Chromium 155 headless driven with puppeteer-core (own profile) running the skill's probes.js unchanged, plus ownership-note contrast, hit-test, clip, overlap and focus-ring probes; 80 combinations, each with a keyboard walk (650 ms per stop around the note). The chrome-devtools MCP browser was unavailable (profile locked by another session).
changedSincePreviousAudit: p.owner ("Copyright © David Bruck" + a.owner__link to https://github.com/gorban/opencode-sandbox, target=_blank, rel="noopener noreferrer", visually hidden " (opens in a new tab)") added after .profile in the sidebar foot of every sidebar page, and after the sign-in panels on signin.html (shown in all three states)
scopeNotes: Level A + AA only (55 criteria). AAA not assessed. 4.1.1 Parsing excluded (removed in WCAG 2.2).
13 criteria re-tested against the change; the other 42 keep their final-763cbac status and note.
Before/after drawer measurements against final-763cbac served read-only on 127.0.0.1:8799.
Text spacing applied with a constructable stylesheet (the CSP blocks the <style> element probes.js injects); no CSP violations.
Link activation tested by keyboard with navigation cancelled in the page; no request was sent to github.com.
No screen reader or speech-input software was run; names and roles verified in Chromium's accessibility snapshot.
Other sidebar pages (approvals, inbox, confirm, states, diff, catalog, thread-2..7) carry the identical markup but were not walked in this run.
final-f1902bc/ is a read-only generated snapshot: make any change in the generator source.

summary.note: Counts cover the 55 Level A + AA criteria and match the coverage table in the HTML report (13 re-tested, 42 carried over). No failures in the changed area; totals unchanged from final-763cbac. Conformance can be claimed once 2.2.1 (backend time limits) is confirmed; not verified with assistive technology.

needsReview.title: Timing Adjustable
needsReview.whatToReview: Approval expiry ("expires 19:30 CST", "expires 16:30 CST") and session expiry (the "Session expired" sign-in state) in the product: can the operator turn off, adjust or extend each limit with at least 20 seconds' warning, or does an exception (essential, real-time, longer than 20 hours) apply?
needsReview.whyOpen: Carried over from final-763cbac; outside this scoped re-audit. The prototype shows both limits but runs neither; their lengths come from the backend.
needsReview.howToConfirm: Leave an approval open near its expiry and leave a session idle. Pass if a warning gives at least 20 seconds and a simple way to extend (at least 10 times), or the limit is adjustable, off, essential, or longer than 20 hours. Fail if it expires silently.

advisories.note: The note adds ~56 px (69 px with text spacing) to the non-scrolling .side__foot. In the drawer layout (below 60rem) at 320x568 the scrolling tree area (.side__scroll) shrinks from 164 to 108 px, and with WCAG text spacing from 138 to 45 px, less than one 48 px tree row. Content stays reachable by scrolling (not a failure). 320x256 is unaffected (page scrolls as a whole).
advisories.suggestion: Let the note scroll with the tree in the drawer layout (e.g. render it at the end of .side__scroll below 60rem), or make the whole drawer scroll on short heights: @media (max-width: 59.99rem) and (max-height: 40rem) { .js .side { overflow-y: auto; grid-template-rows: auto auto auto; } .side__scroll { overflow: visible; } }
acceptanceCriteria: At 320x568 with WCAG text spacing and the Workspace drawer open, .side__scroll (or the drawer) shows at least three tree rows, as in final-763cbac
The note remains reachable by keyboard as the last stop in the drawer

advisories.note: On sign-in at 320x568 (and 320x256 in the Reconnecting state), focusing the link scrolls it flush with the viewport bottom; the 2 px ring drawn 2 px outside extends 4 px below the fold. Top and sides visible; not covered.

On sidebar pages the ownership note (copyright line + external link) sits inside nav#sidebar[aria-label="Workspace"], so landmark navigation presents it as workspace navigation. Allowed; no change needed for conformance.
Pre-existing advisories from final-763cbac still stand; see audits/final-763cbac/reports/wcag-issues.json.
